methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: A deliberate regional initiative to evaluate AI adoption across the Roanoke Valley signals potential movement toward Build It Yourself—but success depends on whether evaluation translates into distributed capability-building or remains consultant-driven and shallow.

signals.title: Virginia Tech tests thermal cameras and AI to warn drivers of animals near roads - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's deployment of AI thermal cameras for wildlife detection demonstrates deep technical capability concentrated in university research centers, but impact on regional AI fluency depends on whether this expertise diffuses to surrounding communities or remains academically siloed.

signals.title: Virginia Orders AI Cybersecurity Plan as States Fill Federal Safety Gaps - PYMNTS.com
signals.signal_reading: A state-mandated AI cybersecurity plan creates uniform policy infrastructure that could enable broad platform-based adoption across agencies, but without deeper capability-building it risks creating shallow, vendor-dependent implementation across all regions.

signals.title: PingThings to expand use of AI platform across Dominion Energy Virginia's grid data - Data Center Dynamics
signals.signal_reading: PingThings' AI platform expansion across Dominion's grid data concentrates advanced analytics capability within utility infrastructure centered in NoVA, creating energy-sector AI expertise that may not transfer to broader workforce development in underserved regions.

signals.title: Roanoke County Career and Technology Center opens - WSLS
signals.signal_reading: Opening a new Career and Technology Center in Roanoke County creates physical infrastructure for hands-on technical skill development in a non-metro region—a necessary but insufficient condition for deep distributed AI capability unless curriculum actively builds AI fluency rather than legacy vocational tracks.
